items.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: one of the first lyrical soloists that I heard that I told dad I wanted to play like was Johnny Hodges.

ctx.x: You had mentioned that you listened to records of course. Who were the people that you were listening to that put you on a path?

Mostly big band players ironically. My dad a lot of big band records, and one of the first lyrical soloists that I heard that I told dad I wanted to play like was Johnny Hodges. And I picked him out. Dad would put on different records, and I would pick him out off every single kind of ballad recording, and say that’s how I want my ballads to sound, Dad. Dizzy Gillespie once told me that I played like a trumpet player. And he suspected that I grew up listening to bebop trumpet players and trumpet players from big…
And who were the first — of course Frank Wess, any other early jazz flute players effect you?
